nodes.summary: For all bit strings $x$ and $w$, the verifier accepts $(x, w)$ iff reading a unary prefix $1^n 0$ off $x$ succeeds, giving $n$ and the rest $r$ of $x$, and then $w$ has at least $2n$ bits, each of the witness colors $c_0, \dots, c_{n-1}$ of $w$ is valid (not $11$), and the edge loop accepts $r$ with the vertex colors $c_0, \dots, c_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: The 3-COLOR verifier as an edge loop

nodes.summary: For bits $a, b$, a bit list $w$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the color codes of the vertices $0, \dots, n$ read from the bit list $a, b, w$ (the list $w$ with $a$ and $b$ prepended) are $(a, b)$ followed by the color codes of the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ read from $w$.
nodes.title: Peeling a vertex off the witness colors

nodes.summary: For a color code $c$, a list $cs$ of color codes and $u, v \in \mathbb{N}$, the edge verdict for $(u + 1, v + 1)$ with vertex colors $c$ followed by $cs$ equals the edge verdict for $(u, v)$ with vertex colors $cs$.
nodes.title: Shifting the edge verdict past the first color

nodes.summary: For a list $cs$ of color codes (pairs of bits), one per vertex, and $u, v \in \mathbb{N}$, the edge $(u, v)$ passes iff $u$ and $v$ are both less than the length of $cs$ and either $u = v$ or entries $u$ and $v$ of $cs$ differ.
nodes.title: Edge verdict

nodes.summary: The verifier statement that begins checking the next edge: if the input stack $X$ is empty it goes to the accepting label, and otherwise it goes to the label that reads the first endpoint of the next edge onto the counter $U$.
nodes.title: Edge-loop start of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: For a list $cs$ of color codes and a bit list $r$, the verdict is true iff $r$ parses as a list of edges, each written as two unary numbers $u$ and $v$ (a number $k$ as $k$ ones, then a zero), and every edge $(u, v)$ of that list passes the edge verdict with vertex colors $cs$.
nodes.title: Edge-loop verdict

nodes.summary: For a list of bits $w$ and natural numbers $i$ and $n$, write $c_w(j)$ for the color code of vertex $j$ in $w$: the pair of bits $2j$ and $2j + 1$ of $w$ (counting from $0$), each read as false past the end of $w$. If $i < n$, then entry $i$ (counting from $0$) of the list $c_w(0), \dots, c_w(n - 1)$ of witness colors is $c_w(i)$.
nodes.title: Reading a witness color

nodes.summary: The verifier has seven stacks: the input $X$ and the witness $W$; the counter $N$ (for the number $n$ of vertices); the color stack $P$ (the $n$ color codes, vertex $0$ on top) and its scratch stack $T$; and the endpoint counters $U$ and $V$.
nodes.title: Stacks of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: The labels are: read the number $n$ of vertices onto the counter stack $N$; load the witness colors onto the scratch stack $T$; move them onto the color stack $P$; start an edge; read its first endpoint onto the counter stack $U$; read its second endpoint onto the counter stack $V$; walk the colors towards both endpoints; for each pair of bits $(a, b)$, walk on towards the farther endpoint holding the nearer one's…
nodes.title: Labels of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: For every list of bits $w$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the witness color codes of the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$ read from $w$ has length $n$.
nodes.title: Number of witness colors

nodes.summary: If the counter stack $N$ is empty, go to the label that moves the codes onto the color stack $P$. Otherwise pop one symbol off $N$ and two bits $a$, $b$ off the witness stack $W$, pushing each onto the scratch stack $T$ as it is popped (so the codes end up reversed on $T$), and go back to the load label; reject instead if $W$ is empty when a bit is due, or if $a$ and $b$ are both $1$ (the invalid code $11$). A…
nodes.title: Load step of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: Given a map $f$ from pairs of bits to labels: if the color stack $P$ is empty, reject (an endpoint lies past the last vertex); otherwise pop two bits $a$, $b$ off $P$, push them onto the scratch stack $T$ in that order (so $b$ ends on top), and go to the label $f(a, b)$. A missing or non-bit symbol is read as $0$.
nodes.title: Moving one color code in the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: The verifier is the program on the seven stacks $X$ (input), $W$ (witness), $N$, $P$, $T$, $U$, $V$, with internal state a bit, that runs as follows. It reads the unary number $n$ off $X$ onto the counter $N$; loads the first $n$ color codes of $W$ onto $T$, rejecting if $W$ runs out or one of these $n$ codes is $11$; moves the bits on top of $T$ onto the color stack $P$; and then repeatedly starts an edge,…
nodes.title: The 3-COLOR verifier machine

nodes.summary: Given a counter stack $c$ and labels $s$ (its own) and $t$ (the next): if the input stack $X$ is empty, reject; otherwise pop a bit off $X$; if it is $1$, push a unit onto $c$ and go back to $s$, and if it is $0$, go to $t$. A symbol of $X$ that is not a bit is read as $0$.
nodes.title: Unary reader of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: Let $l$ and $l'$ be labels, $v$ an internal state and $S$ an assignment of stacks. If executing the verifier's statement at $l$ from state $v$ and stacks $S$ ends at label $l'$, then for some internal state $v'$ and stacks $S'$ the verifier goes in one step from label $l$ with state $v$ and stacks $S$ to label $l'$ with state $v'$ and stacks $S'$.
nodes.title: One step of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: The 3-coloring verifier machine starts at the label that reads the vertex count $n$, written in unary on the input stack $X$, onto the counter stack $N$.
nodes.title: Start label of the 3-coloring verifier

nodes.summary: The type of statements of the verifier as a multi-stack Turing machine in Mathlib's model: each of the seven stacks (the input, the witness, the counter for the number of vertices, the color stack and its scratch stack, and the two endpoint counters) holds symbols of the SAT verifier's alphabet, the labels are the verifier's labels, and the internal state is a single bit.
nodes.title: Statements of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: Let $a \ne b$ be two stacks of the verifier, $S$ an assignment of a list of symbols to every stack, and $p, p', t, t'$ lists of symbols. Setting stack $a$ to $p$, then $b$ to $t$, then $a$ to $p'$, then $b$ to $t'$ gives the same assignment as setting $a$ to $p'$ and then $b$ to $t'$.
nodes.title: Interleaved updates of two stacks of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: The statement pops the top symbol of each of the endpoint counters $U$ and $V$ (a pop from an empty counter leaves it empty) and then moves the next color code $(a, b)$ from the color stack $P$ onto the scratch stack $T$, rejecting if $P$ is empty. It continues at the joint walk again if both counters were nonempty; at the walk towards the endpoint of $U$, holding the color $(a, b)$, if only $U$ was nonempty (so…
nodes.title: One step of the joint walk of the 3-COLOR verifier

nodes.summary: Given a stack $k$ of the 3-COLOR verifier (used as a counter), a label $\ell$ and a pair of bits $(a, b)$ (the color of the nearer endpoint), the statement pops the top symbol of $k$ and then moves the next color code $(a', b')$ from the color stack $P$ onto the scratch stack $T$, rejecting if $P$ is empty. If $k$ was nonempty it continues at $\ell$. Otherwise $(a', b')$ is the color of the farther endpoint, and…
nodes.title: One step of the walk towards the farther endpoint

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
